newSchemaGuard.what: MarketLayerSchema refuses a populated OR partial header when all six quote blocks are unpopulated
newSchemaGuard.why: every other layer refuses an empty claim through .min(1) on its payload collection. The market payload has no collection — it is a fixed record of six sub-blocks — so a market layer could claim to hold content while all six blocks underneath were absent, and validate. This is the softened-populated failure reached through the one door .min(1) does not cover.
newSchemaGuard.bothStatusesOnPurpose: guarding only partial would have left populated as the cheaper way to make the same false claim, making the guard cosmetic
newSchemaGuard.floorNotCeiling: a positive test pins that one populated block over five absences still parses

notAGuard.test: THE SCHEMA CANNOT TELL absent-verified FROM lookup-failed: only the payload can
notAGuard.classification: CHARACTERIZATION TEST, explicitly labelled in the source as a limit rather than a protection
notAGuard.finding: the two determined verdicts share one field set, so swapping them on the adjacency fixture still validates. The schema knows a determination was made, not whether a search ran. Structural distinguishability is carried by the committed payload — a searched scope with an answer about the world, against an unsearched scope with a degraded upstream — not by the type system.
notAGuard.consideredAndRejected: adding a required field to the lookup-failed branch (e.g. the named leg that did not answer) would make the two shapes differ. REJECTED for now on two grounds: it diverges from doc 09's absence block, which shows one uniform shape for all three verdicts; and apps/api already emits a legitimate lookup-failed from an unbuilt synthesis adapter where no upstream leg is involved and both upstreams report ok, so a corroboration rule would false-positive on live behaviour. Flagged for the planner as a contract-level call rather than taken unilaterally on a fixture row.
